claims.claim: Nero blamed the Christians for the fire of Rome and had them tortured
claims.witness: Tacitus, Annals 15.44; retold by Sulpicius Severus, Sacred History II.29

claims.claim: Christus was executed under Tiberius by the procurator Pontius Pilatus
Tacitus wrote after 96
claims.witness: Yonge, preface to Ammianus (his history ends at 96)

claims.claim: The victims were Christians, not Jews as a whole
claims.witness: Tacitus; McGiffert 1890 for; Gibbon and Schiller against

contested_claims.claim: The victims of 64 were Christians, not Jews as a whole
contested_claims.sides: Tacitus and McGiffert (Josephus silent on any attack on the Jews) against Gibbon and Schiller

claims.claim: Claudius expelled Jews who made disturbances at the instigation of Chrestus
Nero punished the Christians, "a new and mischievous superstition"
Secretary to Hadrian, dismissed about 121
Born about 69 or 77
claims.witness: Rolfe: Mommsen 77, Macé 69 (more probable); Thomson-Forester: late in Vespasian's reign

claims.claim: Chrestus is Christ
claims.witness: Rolfe (probable, a chronological error) and Thomson-Forester notes for; Rolfe allows a Jew of that name

contested_claims.sides: For: Rolfe (a chronological error, since the Latin lacks quodam) and the Thomson-Forester notes. Against: no vendored witness holds it; Rolfe only allows that a Jew of that name may be meant

claims.claim: Born in the land of the Assyrians; converted by reading the Scriptures
Hearer of Justin at Rome
Separated from the church after Justin's death, about 172
Taught Aeons, condemned marriage, denied Adam's salvation
claims.witness: Irenaeus I.28.1 (opponent); Hippolytus, Refutation VIII, following Irenaeus

claims.claim: Founder of the Encratites
claims.witness: Eusebius and Jerome for; McGiffert, from Irenaeus, against

claims.claim: Made the Diatessaron, widely read in the Syriac churches
claims.witness: Eusebius IV.29; Hogg, anf09 introduction; Theodoret (McGiffert, Hogg)

claims.claim: Diatessaron first written in Syriac
claims.witness: Zahn for, and a growing majority per Hogg; Harnack for Greek, favoured by McGiffert

claims.claim: Harnack's outline of his life: twice at Rome, broke about 172
claims.witness: McGiffert for Harnack against Zahn; Hogg: left Rome for Mesopotamia

contested_claims.sides: Eusebius and Jerome make him founder; McGiffert reads Irenaeus as tracing them to Saturninus and Marcion

contested_claims.claim: The Diatessaron was first written in Syriac
contested_claims.sides: Zahn, followed by Lightfoot, Hilgenfeld and Fuller, and per Hogg a growing majority, for Syriac; Harnack for Greek, whose reasons McGiffert calls very strong

Harnack (converted about 150, East, back to Rome, broke about 172), whose main positions McGiffert says Harnack's arguments seem fully to establish, against Zahn (once at Rome, became a heretic in the East); Hogg has him leave Rome for Mesopotamia after Justin's death

claims.claim: Taught at Edessa; skilled disputant in Syriac; wrote against the Marcionites
The Book of the Laws of Countries gives his argument, written by a disciple
First a Valentinian, then left
claims.witness: Eusebius IV.30 and McGiffert (with Hort) against Epiphanius 56 and Barhebraeus (first orthodox, then Valentinian)

claims.claim: Resisted a companion of the emperor who urged him to deny he was a Christian
Born about 155, died about 223
claims.witness: Chronicle of Edessa and Barhebraeus, via McGiffert

claims.claim: His son Harmonius made Syriac hymns; Ephrem wrote to his metres
Ephrem knew him only through his followers

contested_claims.claim: The order of his life: Valentinian first, or orthodox first
contested_claims.sides: Eusebius (Valentinian, then left it), whom McGiffert thinks may well be right, against Epiphanius and Barhebraeus (orthodox, then Valentinian)

claims.claim: Exiled to Sardinia in 235 with the bishop Pontianus
claims.witness: Liberian catalogue in the book of 354; McGiffert (Lipsius: indisputable)

claims.claim: Wrote the Refutation of All Heresies
Callistus was a slave, banker and convict who rose to be bishop
claims.witness: Hippolytus, Refutation IX (one hostile witness); McGiffert: groundwork true, greatly overdrawn

claims.claim: He was a rival bishop to Callistus
Bishop of Portus
claims.witness: Tradition; MacMahon for; Döllinger and McGiffert against

claims.claim: The 1551 statue is his
Buried on the Tiburtine Road
claims.witness: Depositio martyrum in the book of 354

contested_claims.sides: MacMahon, Bunsen, Wordsworth and the later tradition for; Döllinger against Portus but for a bishopric; McGiffert: "quite worthless", a presbyter set up as rival bishop

claims.claim: Made rival bishop at Rome in 251 against Cornelius
claims.witness: Cornelius in Eusebius VI.43; Cyprian; Dionysius in VI.45

claims.claim: Exacted an oath at the Eucharist
claims.witness: Cornelius in Eusebius VI.43 (one hostile witness)

claims.claim: Hid during the persecution and refused to help
Clinic baptism
On the Trinity is orthodox
Died a martyr under Valerian
Acesius at Nicaea and Constantine's ladder
claims.witness: Socrates I.10, from Auxanon, a Novatian presbyter at Nicaea (I.13); retold by Sozomen I.22

claims.claim: His church lasted into the sixth century

contested_claims.claim: Novatian died a martyr under Valerian
contested_claims.sides: Socrates of Constantinople for; Valesius against (the Novatian martyrdom book called him a confessor)

contested_claims.claim: Novatian shirked his duty in the persecution
contested_claims.sides: Cornelius for; McGiffert against (calumny); Neander: ascetic withdrawal

claims.claim: Pontius, Cyprian's deacon, wrote the Life and Passion of Cyprian
Shared Cyprian's exile at Curubis

absent_details.note: Coxe says he is said to have died a martyr, and Richardson gives about 260; neither names a source

claims.claim: Rescued from soldiers by wedding guests under Decius
claims.witness: Dionysius, letter to Germanus, in Eusebius VI.40 (his own defence)

claims.claim: Pupil of Origen, head of the school, bishop from about 247
Wrote to Novatian urging him to withdraw
Christians nursed the sick in the plague
claims.witness: Dionysius in Eusebius VII.22 (one witness, a bishop praising his flock)

claims.claim: The Revelation is by a John other than the apostle
claims.witness: Dionysius in Eusebius VII.25 (his judgment from style)

claims.claim: His Refutation and Defence ended the dispute with Dionysius of Rome
claims.witness: Robertson, introduction to Athanasius, De Sententia Dionysii

claims.claim: Died in the twelfth year of Gallienus

contested_claims.claim: The apostle John did not write the Revelation
contested_claims.sides: Dionysius (a holy man named John wrote it, but not the apostle) and those before him who rejected the book and gave it to Cerinthus, against the traditional reading that the apostle wrote it; Dionysius adds that many brethren held the book in high esteem
